ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders at or above 25%, and authorized signatories against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list (applicable given Swift Wire and Stripe payment rails), EU consolidated financial sanctions list, FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdiction lists, and South African domestic designations issued under FICA ss28A-28B and POCDATARA. Politically Exposed Person determination is governed by the FICA s1 definition of a prominent individual, including close relatives and close associates; enhanced due diligence, ongoing transaction monitoring, and risk rating must be documented and maintained in a FICA s42 Risk Management and Compliance Programme (RMCP).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services Company Registry Portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za), operated by the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in any of South Africa's 11 official languages; non-Latin script names must be accompanied by a Latin-script transliteration for entry on the CIPC register. The proposed name must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name or protected trademark, must not mislead the public, and must satisfy the distinctiveness and prohibited-name criteria set out in Regulations 11-13 of the Companies Regulations, 2011.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of a name reservation application, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the CIPC Registrar within 10 business days through the CIPC e-Services portal; if the reconsideration is denied, the aggrieved applicant may institute a complaint to the Companies Tribunal for a determination under s160 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008 within 30 days of the adverse decision. A reserved name cannot be extended beyond its statutory six-month validity; the applicant may re-file a fresh name reservation application via Form CoR 9.1 after expiry or immediately after a final rejection using a corrected, distinct name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office services are permissible as the business and postal address, but the registered office must be a physical South African street address capable of receiving legal service of process under Companies Act s23(2)-(3). A PO Box or private bag is prohibited as the registered office. For this non-licensed, low-risk software middleware entity, a serviced office or registered-office address with a real street location and physical access is compliant; a wholly virtual, unstaffed address without physical substance is not compliant.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: under 5% annual probability in the first year for this low-risk, non-licensed software sector. Probability increases to approximately 10-15% after VAT and income tax registration if the registered office fails commercial-substance indicators (absence of signage, records, or personnel) or following a FICA RMCP compliance review; unannounced physical inspections may be conducted by CIPC inspectors, SAPS officers enforcing the FIC Act, and SARS officials where substance indicators are triggered.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) – national tax portal and filing system: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated company carrying on a South African enterprise must register with SARS for income tax and VAT. Step 1: Register as a non-resident company via SARS eFiling using the IT77 (Non-Resident Company Registration) application together with certified incorporation documents (Memorandum of Incorporation, Certificate of Incorporation, proof of foreign registration) and a local business address. Step 2: SARS issues an Income Tax Reference Number. Step 3: Register for VAT under Section 23 of the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991 using form VAT101 (or VAT101e for non-resident suppliers of electronic services) once taxable turnover exceeds or is expected to exceed the compulsory threshold; voluntary VAT registration is available from the R50,000 threshold. A foreign external company may also register through the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) and obtain a SARS Customs/PRN code for import-export purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (A Pty Ltd is a resident company subject to the standard 27% corporate income tax rate on worldwide income; a non-resident company is taxed on South Africa-sourced income only. No territorial pass-through applies.)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: South Africa does not operate a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification follows the legal incorporation form and the place of central management-and-control. Electable regimes available include: VAT group registration under Section 51 of the VAT Act for connected entities; the participation exemption for qualifying foreign dividends and foreign branch income under Section 9D and Section 9E of the Income Tax Act; the accounting-period election for provisional taxpayers; and mandatory hybrid mismatch rules under Sections 9DA to 9E of the Income Tax Act, with reportable arrangement disclosure for cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 (ZAR 1 million) compulsory registration threshold applied over the preceding 12 months or expected next 12 months; voluntary registration from R50,000 (ZAR); zero threshold for non-resident suppliers of electronic, digital and gaming-security services under the SARS electronic-services VAT registration regime
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, central digital stamping or compulsory API stampede currently exists. SARS recognises paper, PDF, EDI and XML invoices and has introduced a voluntary e-invoicing framework aligned to OECD and CIAT standards, transitioning toward the SARS E-Invoicing Pilot (2024-2025). Large enterprises may use the SARS eFiling API to submit VAT201 returns and data extracts; record retention of 5 years applies under Section 18 of the VAT Act, and invoices must contain the mandatory VAT fields (vendor name, VAT number, invoice number, supply date, tax invoice wording, consideration, VAT amount).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act, exported goods are zero-rated where the exporter holds a customs Bill of Entry (SAD500) evidencing export before or at dispersal and provides proof of shipment abroad within the prescribed period. Under Section 11(2)(l), exported services (including gaming anti-cheat software licences, kernel-level middleware subscriptions and cloud-based integrity services) are zero-rated where the supply is to a non-resident for use wholly outside South Africa, the services are not supplied to a resident, and the supply is not physically performed in South Africa; connected-person exclusions in Section 11(2)(l)(iii) require market-value consideration. Exporters may also claim zero-rating for direct exports of the embedded anti-cheat SDK to foreign gaming studios with simultaneous ownership transfer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD500 Bill of Entry) finally cleared by SARS Customs
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / transport evidence proving physical movement to a foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a South African authorised-dealer bank account
Commercial invoice, software licence or SaaS agreement proving the non-resident customer and the transaction's commercial substance
Digital-evidence package for middleware exports (SDK delivery logs, activation keys, and end-user destination metadata) supporting the Section 11 export clawback review
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Under Section 59 and Section 60(1A)(a) of the VAT Act, incorrect zero-rating attracts an additional 'non-declaration' penalty of up to 195% of the assessed VAT together with interest at 15% per annum under the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011. Criminal prosecution for deliberate export fraud may impose fines of up to R10 million and imprisonment of up to 10 years. SARS has a retrospective 5-year audit window and may claw back input tax credits and zero-rated output treatment where the exporter fails to produce the mandatory SAD500, shipping and foreign-currency receipt evidence. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days triggers suspicion under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 and may invalidate the zero-rating claim or trigger additional assessments with understatement penalties of 35% to 200% for 'substantial understatement' or 'gross negligence' findings.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), the statutorily designated exchange-control administrator under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933 and the Exchange Control Regulations, read with the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA). All foreign-exchange transactions of a South African resident company must be routed through an authorised dealer, being a registered South African commercial bank that SARB has licensed to operate the national payment and foreign-exchange clearing infrastructure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African Rand (ZAR) is fully convertible for bona fide current-account transactions: trade in goods, services, software licensing, royalties, interest, and dividends remitted from after-tax profits require no prior SARB approval provided the resident effects the payment or receipt through an authorised dealer. Inward foreign direct investment into an unlisted private company is liberalised under the active-monitoring framework: the non-resident shareholder may subscribe for shares without prior FinSurv approval, but the inward capital transfer must be reported electronically by the authorised dealer and the shares issued only after the funds land in a South African account. Capital-account outflows remain the principal hurdle: loans to non-residents, offshore accounts, and investments by the South African resident outside South Africa are subject to formal approval, documentary substantiation, and the prohibition on loop structures (South African resident participation held abroad). Profit remittance hurdles are limited to verifiable form: dividends may be freely remitted once the dividend withholding tax (20%, or treaty-reduced rate) is accounted for and the company holds a valid SARS Tax Compliance Status Pin, a board resolution, audited annual financial statements, and proof of solvency per section 46 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Branch or royalty remittances require associated SARS filings and the applicable withholding tax on royalties (15% or treaty-reduced). There is no general blocked-rand regime for current returns on non-resident investment; blocked-rand mechanisms arise only in legacy emigration contexts and are irrelevant to a standard gaming-software export company.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory baseline under SARB CEMAD and the Exchange Control Regulations, as amended by Amendment No. 30/2021 effective 1 January 2022: export proceeds in respect of goods must be received in South Africa within 180 days of shipment, and service or software-licensing proceeds within 180 days of invoicing. The authorised dealer may, on application, extend the 180-day window to a maximum of 365 days where the underlying commercial contract justifies extended settlement and the exporter is fully tax-compliant. Mandatory conversion ratio: 0% — the 2021 liberalisation abolished any obligation to convert export proceeds into rand; the company may retain 100% of its export receipts in a designated foreign currency account (FCA) held with a South African authorised dealer. Repatriation to the South African FCA remains compulsory, and set-offs of foreign receivables against foreign payables require prior dealer approval. Receipts from the anti-cheat-software licensing business are classified as export of services and intellectual property and must be documented with signed licensing agreements, commercial invoices, delivery/acceptance evidence, and a valid SARS tax-compliance standing at the moment of receipt.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary account-holding rail. A South African resident private company is legally prohibited from opening or maintaining a foreign bank or electronic-money-institution (EMI) account without prior FinSurv approval, and the Exchange Control Regulations mandate that all foreign-currency receipts and payments be cleared through a South African authorised dealer. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, Mercury, Airwallex, Currencycloud) are not authorised dealers and cannot lawfully serve as the repository of export proceeds or as the exclusive paying agent for outbound current payments. Permissible ancillary role: an offshore EMI may act as a supplementary collection node for card-acquiring flows or marketplaces only if the funds are swept into the company's authorised-dealer FCA within the applicable 180-day (or dealer-approved 365-day) repatriation deadline; the arrangement must be pre-disclosed to the bank's transactional-compliance group and formalised in the treasury policy. The target payment rail 'Stripe' is acceptable at the collection layer because Stripe Payments South Africa (Pty) Ltd operates as a local regulated payment-service provider settling ZAR into the company's resident bank account; Stripe itself is not a foreign-currency clearing path.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: There is no universal statutory mandate requiring all directors to appear physically in-branch. FICA Permit remote and non-face-to-face customer due diligence where the bank applies reliable independent electronic verification, video-identification, and source-of-documentation checks; the four major South African banks routinely onboard a standard low-risk private company (ISIC 6201 software exporter) without a physical site visit. Practical requirements: certified CIPC registration documents (including Memorandum of Incorporation and amended entities report), board resolution authorising account opening, register of members/beneficial-ownership disclosure (25% or more natural-person UBOs), and notarised and apostilled passport copies plus proof of residential address for every foreign director and shareholder. Foreign directors are commonly invited to a Teams/telepresence compliance interview; the bank may, at its discretion, require physical appearance where the jurisdiction of the beneficial owner is on a FATF grey list, where a director is a politically exposed person, or where the beneficial-ownership chain cannot be independently verified. A local professional introducer (South African attorney or auditor) materially accelerates onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-ownership opacity: the 25%-or-more ultimate natural person of the (Pty) Ltd cannot be evidenced because an intermediate foreign holding entity sits in the chain without substantiation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete CIPC shareholder register and Beneficial Ownership Register filed with CIPC; certified share certificates for each class; notarised passports of all ultimate natural-person UBOs; corporate diagram with percentage interests at every tier; constitutional documents and register of members of the foreign intermediate holding entity; and a compliance attestation signed by the directors per FIC Guidance Note on beneficial ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds red flag on the inward foreign share capital subscription: a single large inbound remittance from a non-resident investor lacking an audited financial trail or unexplained rapid accumulation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Two years of audited financial statements of the investing shareholder or, for a high-net-worth individual, a certified net-worth statement; tax residence certificate and foreign tax clearance; 12 months of bank statements evidencing lawful accumulation of the funds; executed share subscription agreement and board-approved allotment resolution; independent valuation certificate for the private-company equity; and a client-narrative letter from the remitting bank confirming the originator of the SWIFT MT103.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible-trade justification risk: the bank classifies gaming anti-cheat middleware licensing as high-risk IP royalty flow because the exported product is software-as-a-service with no physical bill of lading, raising the concern of disguised capital flight or transfer mispricing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master software license, SaaS subscription, and end-user licence agreements naming the customers and payment terms; commercial invoices and delivery/acceptance records; intercompany or third-party pricing benchmark to evidence arm's-length royalty rates; ISIC 6201 scope declaration; annual audited financial statements segmenting software revenue; a legal-opinion memorandum confirming title, ownership, and exportability of the anti-cheat integrity middleware; and SARS IP classification records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and PEP screening hits: a director or material customer shares a name with a listed UN, EU, OFAC, or FIC sanctions designation, or qualifies as a politically exposed person requiring enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed FICA PEP declaration for each director and UBO; verified biographical CVs; certified government-issued identity documentation; sanctions-screening explanation letter distinguishing the entity from the listed person; and, where a customer is located in a higher-risk jurisdiction, end-customer due diligence comprising a trade rationale letter, beneficial-ownership details, and confirmation that the anti-cheat software carries no dual-use, surveillance, or prohibited military application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-compliance gate: the authorised dealer cannot execute a dividend remittance, royalty payment, or large outward current transfer because the company's SARS Tax Compliance Status Pin is not issued, is expired, or fails the SARS verification threshold.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid SARS Tax Compliance Status Pin (TCS PIN) covering the remittance period; appointment of the public officer on SARS Form; five-year corporate tax filing and assessment history; VAT registration and supporting return filings; provisional tax and payroll (PAYE/UIF/SDL) submissions; and an express board confirmation that the remittance respect sections 22 and 23D of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 and the CEMAD current-payment documentary standard.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for the non-resident equity injection into ZA_PTY_LTD: (1) The non-resident investor instructs a SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA equivalent) to the company's authorised-dealer bank, quoting the South African SEF/BOP purpose code for inward direct investment in equity (category 'I' direct investment, equity/DI) and referencing the executed share subscription agreement. (2) The authorised dealer credits the funds to a non-resident inward-capital suspense escrow; where remitted in foreign currency, the funds are held in a non-resident Foreign Currency Account until conversion; where remitted in rand, they are held in the escrow until the share allotment is documented. (3) On presentation of the board allotment resolution, the updated register of members, the amended MOI (if any), and proof of lodgement with CIPC, the dealer converts at the prevailing market rate and releases the net proceeds to the operating ZAR account. (4) The authorised dealer files the inward FDI declaration with FinSurv electronically through the Currency and Exchanges (COFE) platform; no prior SARB approval is required for unlisted private-company equity from a non-resident, provided no loop structure exists and no inward funds derive from any South African-resident source held abroad. (5) Verification bundle: board resolutions, amended incorporation documents, share certificates, complete beneficial-ownership filing, source-of-funds documentation, and the dealer's conversion ticket. All bank fees, conversion spreads, and the inward-transfer handling charge are compliant deductions apportioned to the company's P&L.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for outbound treasury activity: (a) Foreign-currency current payments (global cloud-hosting fees, subcontract development, non-resident contractor salaries, marketing procurement): SWIFT MT103 routed through the authorised dealer, each payment screened against sanctions lists and accompanied by the underlying contract and commercial invoice; the bank records the BOP service-payment purpose code and, for royalties or IP licences, applies the 15% withholding (or treaty-reduced rate) and remits the tax to SARS before releasing the net amount. (b) Physical trade settlements (server hardware, anti-cheat appliance components): documentary letter of credit opened through the commercial bank's trade desk, or SWIFT MT103 with commercial invoice, transport document, packing list, and inspection certificates; ZAR-denominated domestic legs clear through the South African Multiple Option Settlement system. (c) Any outward payment above the dealer's low-value exemption threshold must be documented in COFE and, where capital in nature, requires FinSurv formality; the treasury policy must forbid speculative transfers and require a fully evidenced economic purpose for every instruction. (d) The Stripe collection rail settles net card-acquiring proceeds into the ZAR operating account on a T+2-to-T+5 cycle and is expressly outside the foreign-exchange compliance perimeter; Stripe is used solely as a merchant acquiring layer, never as a foreign-currency clearing or account-holding mechanism.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forward exchange contracts (FECs/DFCs): permissible without SARB approval for documented transactional exposure arising from invoiced software-licence exports and contracted foreign-currency payables, for tenors of up to 12 months, renewable upon re-verification of the underlying exposure; this is the primary hedging instrument for the anti-cheat-software subscription revenue cycle.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS): permissible through the authorised dealer where the company enters foreign-currency-denominated debt or capital structures evidenced by loan agreements, board resolutions, and financial projections; used to hedge both principal and interest exposure of cross-border funding.

Outright currency swaps (FX spot-forward swap combinations): permissible as synthetic matched-funding and rolling-hedge structures under the authorised dealer's market-risk mandate, provided the trades hedge bona fide commercial exposure and never create a speculative open position.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF): generally not permissible as a primary onshore hedge because SARB requires the underlying exposure to be demonstrated and an onshore deliverable already exists; offshore ZAR NDFs introduce an unauthorised cross-border component and will be accepted only in exceptional balance-sheet circumstances with prior FinSurv approval. The treasury policy excludes NDFs from the standard hedge programme.

Zero-cost collars and purchased FX options: not generally permissible without FinSurv approval because option premiums constitute a capital outflow and SARB historically permits only premium-free or cost-symmetric structures; the company's treasury policy should rely on forwards and swaps and seek ruling-level authorisation before any option-based strategy.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (ITA s5 read with s11; reduced from 28% for years of assessment commencing on or after 1 April 2022; the 27% applies to the (Pty) Ltd's taxable income from the gaming anti-cheat middleware business)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Section 11D R&D incentive: 150% deduction of qualifying R&D expenditure (prior SARS/DSI pre-approval required; applies to kernel-level anti-cheat and integrity middleware development); Section 11(gB): 3-year write-off of computer software development costs (25%, 25%, 50%); Section 12C: capital allowances on plant/machinery; Section 12E: Small Business Corporation rate schedule (0-21% for qualifying companies with annual turnover below ZAR 20 million); Section 11C learnership allowances; the effective rate for a fully incentivised qualifying R&D developer is depressed to approx. 18-24%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime_note: No statutory time limit on assessed losses carried forward by trading companies under ITA s20; the figure of 5 represents the SARS prescription window for additional assessments of 5 years (TAA s99/ s99A) and is the conservative horizon for using the carryforward; s20A loss restriction applies where there is a change of ownership without a qualifying trade.
